1 172/2018 dated 29.8.2018 as the predicate / Scheduled Offence.
2. The petitioner is a citizen of United Kingdom, however, his parents are stated to be Indian passport holders, holding property and residing in India.
It is stated that the petitioner's family has deep roots in the Indian society.
The petitioner also has two grand-children who also reside in India.

3. The petitioner seeks that the impugned LOC/s be suspended inasmuch as the petitioner is required to urgently travel to United Kingdom in view of his allegedly serious medical condition (viz.
"Nasal Polyps").
It is submitted that on account thereof, the petitioner has lost his sense of smell and taste.
It is submitted that the petitioner made efforts to have the said condition treated locally

;
however, the same was not to his satisfaction.
It is submitted that his present position is such that he has to undergo surgery as advised by his Doctor, Prof. Claire Hopkins in the ENT Department of the Guy's Hospital, Harley Street, London.
4. The said prayer is vehemently opposed by learned counsel for Enforcement Directorate (ED) and HDFC Bank.
They submit that the petitioner's version as regards his medical condition has been contrived so that he can evade the jurisdiction of this Court in the guise thereof.

They further submit that the petitioner, through his companies has availed huge loans and the outstanding amount payable is to the tune of Rs.150 Crores.
5.
It is contended that the petitioner is a flight risk and it would be highly prejudicial to his ongoing prosecution if he is allowed to travel abroad.
6. During the course of hearing it transpires that the Supreme Court, vide This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 29/06/2025 at 23:58:33 order dated 18.12.2019, in proceedings concerning the grant of bail to the petitioner, has inter-alia directed / taken note of the undertaking of the petitioner that "he will not travel without leave of the Trial Court".
7.
In the circumstances, it would be apposite for the petitioner to move an application before the Trial Court seeking permission to travel abroad.

If and when such permission is granted, this Court would consider the request of the petitioner for suspension of the LOC/s.
8.
At this stage, learned senior counsel for the petitioner submits that the requisite application shall be forthwith filed before the Trial Court.
Let the same be considered and disposed of by the Trial Court expeditiously, preferably within a period of two weeks from the date of filing thereof.

9. List on 29.05.2025.
SACHIN DATTA, J MAY 9, 2025/cl
